provenance.built_from: the fixture's required_beats, read against the source text (Dickens, A Christmas Carol (PG #46)) and the event definition in src/extraction/pass-events.ts
provenance.blind_to: whether a candidate matched the beat. The classification was made from the beat and the definition; the recorded runs were consulted only afterwards, to compute the numbers.
provenance.author: hand-annotated (a manual read, not a judge pass — a judge pass can replace it and be compared against it)

inclusion_rule.definition: pass-events.ts: "An event is one thing that HAPPENS or CHANGES: an action, an arrival, a decision made aloud, a death, a transformation, a promise. Not a description, not a mood, not a standing fact."
inclusion_rule.non_eventful_when: the beat, as the fixture words it, contains no action, speech act, arrival or change of state or knowledge at all
eventful_when: the beat contains any happening, even alongside a mood or a description
in doubt — a beat is excluded only when it is clearly not an event, so the list errs toward a larger denominator and a lower recall_eventful
inclusion_rule.note: Classified by the beat as written, not by what the source narrates nearby. This says nothing about whether the beat matters to the story — "Cinderella does not ask to go" matters a great deal — only about whether an extractor obeying its own prompt can emit it.

non_eventful.text: Scrooge does not recognize anyone they describe, and does not think to ask whose death it is
non_eventful.why: A recognition that does not occur and a question Scrooge does not ask.

non_eventful.text: Scrooge is horrified by the scene but still does not connect it to himself
non_eventful.why: A feeling, plus a connection Scrooge does not make.

non_eventful.text: Tiny Tim's little crutch is kept, without its owner, in a corner
non_eventful.why: An object standing in a corner.

non_eventful.text: Bob, terrified for a moment, is then astonished into delight
non_eventful.why: Two feelings in sequence, as the beat is written. The source gives Bob a physical reaction (he trembles and edges toward the ruler), so a beat worded around that would be an event; this one is not.

borderline_kept_eventful.text: Scrooge is overcome with penitence and grief and casts his eyes down, ashamed
borderline_kept_eventful.why: Mostly feeling, but the beat names a gesture (he casts his eyes down). Kept.

borderline_kept_eventful.text: Scrooge understands, without being told, that no one anywhere has shed one genuine tear for this man
borderline_kept_eventful.why: An inference of the fixture author's, but a change in what Scrooge knows. Kept.

borderline_kept_eventful.text: the Cratchit household is quiet and subdued; Tiny Tim has died
borderline_kept_eventful.why: Half atmosphere, but it asserts a death. Kept.

borderline_kept_eventful.text: the narrator closes: Scrooge became as good a friend, as good a master, and as good a man as the good old city knew; and it was always said of him that he knew how to keep Christmas well, if any man alive possessed the knowledge
borderline_kept_eventful.why: The narrator's closing summary; "became" is a transformation. Kept.
